# Environment

A YAML document with `apiVersion: solaria.sh/v1alpha1` and `kind: Environment`. The other resources are [Agent](agent.md), [Target](target.md), [McpServer](mcp-server.md) and [Vault](vault.md), and the [concepts](../concepts.md) explain how they fit together.

## Fields

The same rules are in the [JSON Schema](../../schemas/v1alpha1/), which `solaria schema` prints for editors. Paths use `.` for nested fields, `[]` for list items and `<name>` for map keys you choose.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `apiVersion` | `solaria.sh/v1alpha1` | yes | API version of this resource. |
| `kind` | `Environment` | yes | Kind of this resource. |
| `metadata` | object | yes | Identifies the Environment. The name default is reserved for the built-in sandbox. |
| `metadata.name` | string | yes | Unique name per kind. Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting and ending with a letter or digit, at most 63 characters. Matches `^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?$`. |
| `metadata.labels` | map of strings |  | Labels for selecting resources, for example from a Target's agents.selector. |
| `metadata.annotations` | map of strings |  | Notes about how the resource is operated rather than what it is, such as an agent's owner, trigger or target autonomy. Keys are like label keys; values are any text. They're never part of a digest or sent to a host, so changing one changes nothing deployed. solaria status -o json shows an agent's. |
| `spec` | object | yes | Describes the sandbox. |
| `spec.packages` | object |  | Packages to install, by package manager, in each manager's own pin syntax. |
| `spec.packages.apt` | list of strings |  | APT packages. |
| `spec.packages.cargo` | list of strings |  | Cargo crates. |
| `spec.packages.gem` | list of strings |  | Ruby gems. |
| `spec.packages.go` | list of strings |  | Go modules, installed with go install. |
| `spec.packages.npm` | list of strings |  | npm packages, installed globally. |
| `spec.packages.pip` | list of strings |  | pip packages. |
| `spec.network` | object |  | Outbound network access. When omitted, access is limited to the hosts the agents need. |
| `spec.network.mode` | `limited` or `unrestricted` |  | limited (only allowed hosts) or unrestricted. |
| `spec.network.allow` | list of strings |  | Extra hosts the sandbox may reach in limited mode. Each matches `^(\*\.)?[A-Za-z0-9]([-A-Za-z0-9]*[A-Za-z0-9])?(\.[A-Za-z0-9]([-A-Za-z0-9]*[A-Za-z0-9])?)*$`. |
| `spec.network.packageManagers` | boolean |  | Allows the package managers' registries in limited mode. |
| `spec.resources` | object |  | Memory and disk caps, where the placement allows them. |
| `spec.resources.memory` | string |  | Memory cap, such as 8Gi. Matches `^[0-9]+(Ki\|Mi\|Gi\|Ti)?$`. |
| `spec.resources.disk` | string |  | Disk cap, such as 10Gi. Matches `^[0-9]+(Ki\|Mi\|Gi\|Ti)?$`. |
| `spec.image` | string |  | Replaces the generated sandbox image: a container image reference, or a path to a Dockerfile relative to this file. Only container placements accept it. |
| `spec.isolation` | `srt` |  | Wraps each run in an OS-level sandbox, on placements that don't have one of their own. srt runs the process placement's launcher inside Anthropic's sandbox-runtime, which must be installed: writes are limited to the run's scratch folders and the inputs the agent may write, and the network to the hosts the agents need. macOS and Linux only. |
